thread:
Maya: Heads-up — Sales reported a QuantaHealth complaint: p95 has jumped ~4x since last night's deploy. Putting intake here to decide priority and scope. Ticket + graphs linked below.
Diego: https://support.redwood.example/t/QUANTA-987 latency graph attached. Customer on Dedicated (eu-west-1), model: gpt-large-quant. Their SLA is 200ms p95. Seeing ~800ms spikes around 02:10-02:30 UTC. QPS ~10–15.
Priya: Thanks. Quick triage questions: 1) did the deploy include a routing change or quantization/profile change? 2) can we reproduce in staging? 3) proposed launch criteria to close the ticket?
Liam: No routing changes in the release notes; infra pushed kernel updates and we rolled a new runtime image (runt-v2.14). Might be a kernel/path change. I can start reproducing with a load test on a copy of their config.
Diego: Sales log says we moved the model to a quantized variant during the deploy: `gpt-large-quant-v2`. Customer confirmed they saw the jump post-deploy.
Jules: Possible culprits: 1) quantization interaction with KV-cache causing slow warmup, 2) kernel selection falling back to fallback path under certain sequence lengths, 3) autoscaler thresholds mis-tuned so cold instances serve extra latency.
eng-oncall-bot: deploy-bot reported: PROD deploy runt-v2.14 completed by infra at 2026-03-20T01:45:12Z
Liam: I'll try a targeted repro using their request shape + sequence length distribution. Need a redacted sample request.
Diego: Customer sent a redacted payload: ``{
  "input": "Summarize recent claims for patient X...",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "context_length": 1024
}``
Priya: For prioritization: I'm proposing P1 customer-impact (SLA breached for a paid Dedicated customer). Launch/closure criteria: 1) root cause identified and mitigation deployed to prod or rollback executed, 2) p95 back under 250ms for 2 hours under comparable traffic, 3) customer comms within 4 hours with ETA. Agree?
Maya: Agreed on criteria. If it's a kernel/runtime regression we might prefer rollback to keep customer online while we root-cause. Product needs an estimated ETA for rollback vs hotfix.
Jules: I can scope both: rollback to runt-v2.13 (fast path) — ~30–45m to validate and canary. Hotfix depends on cause; if it's cache warmup we can push a config to pre-warm/preserve KV cache per node (15–60m). If it's kernel selection we need deeper debugging (4+ hrs).
Priya: Ok that's helpful. Product asks engineering for an initial runbook: steps for canary rollback, impact on other customers, metrics to watch. Also need a changelog entry for compliance.
Liam: I'll start a repro in our staging cluster using their qps and payload. Will post logs + flame graphs within 45m. If I confirm regression with runt-v2.14 I'll draft the rollback steps.
Diego: Customer wants hourly updates. They asked about SLA credits if we can't meet SLA this week. Please keep that in mind for comms.
Maya: Negotiation note: Sales requested us to escalate timeline for fix. Product balancing with two other P1s this sprint. If rollback is low-risk we'll do it immediately; if high-risk we'll negotiate a 2-hour interim workaround (route them to alternate pool) and schedule rollback.
Jules: Action items: 1) Liam repro + logs (assigned), 2) Jules prepare rollback canary playbook (assigned), 3) Maya to draft customer update + coordinate with sales (assigned), 4) Priya to create backlog ticket with acceptance criteria & SLA note.
Priya: I'll open PROD ticket REDWOOD-QUANTA-987-HOTFIX with ACs and link this thread. ETA for initial customer update: 45m.
deploy-bot: canary rollback run created: canary-rollback-2213456795 (pending validation)
Liam: Repro started. Early sign: p50 similar but p95 sensitive to sequence length ~900–1100 tokens. Attaching first heap profile in the ticket.
Priya: Keeping scope narrow: immediate goal is restore SLA; long-term: add synthetic monitors for quantized-variants and a gating test in CI to catch regressions between runt releases.
Maya: Final note — if rollback completes, we still need a postmortem and a decision on whether to pin QuantaHealth to previous runtime until we get a verifiably-stable release.
Priya: Thanks team. I'll post the ticket link + customer update when sent.
Diego: Customer acked they received the staging proof-of-concept and appreciate quick response. :thumbsup:
Maya: Closing this thread for now — follow-ups will be in the PROD ticket.
